newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-BENETTON HIT AS TOP TECHNICAL MEN QUIT.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-BENETTON HIT AS TOP TECHNICAL MEN QUIT.

text.p: The Benetton Formula One Grand Prix team confirmed on Tuesday that both technical director Ross Brawn and chief designer Rory Byrne had quit.

Brawn, the man behind the technical successes of the team's championship-winning seasons of 1994 and 1995, is expected to join Ferrari and resume his successful relationship with double world champion Michael Schumacher of Germany.
Byrne, a long-serving member at Benetton, is retiring to concentrate on other interests outside the sport.
Their positions are being taken by chief engineer Pat Symonds, who steps up to become technical director, and Nick Wirth, who joined Benetton in 1995 following the collapse of his own team Simtek.

"I am delighted to take on this new challenge," said Symonds. "Having worked as race engineer with both Michael Schumacher and Jean Alesi I am looking forward to taking my role that important step further and to help regain the world championship title."

Italian Flavio Briatore, Benetton managing director, said: "I am fully confident that this new technical structure combined with the continuity of Jean Alesi and Gerhard Berger as the Mild Seven Benetton Renault drivers for the 1997 season will bring us a winning formula."
